report.tagline: AI voice company that turns text into lifelike speech in 70+ languages, clones voices, dubs videos and powers talking AI agents.
report.simpleSummary: ElevenLabs makes computer voices that sound like real people. You paste text and it reads it aloud with emotion, in your own cloned voice or one of thousands of others. It can also translate a video into Hindi or Spanish while keeping the speaker's voice. Companies use it to build AI phone agents that talk to customers, and creators use it for audiobooks, YouTube and podcasts.

overview.whatItDoes: ElevenLabs builds AI audio models and sells them through apps and an API. Its main products are text to speech, voice cloning, dubbing, speech to text, music and sound effects, and a platform for voice agents that hold live phone or app conversations.
howItWorks: Text to speech: paste text, pick a voice and get natural audio, with control over emotion and pace using models like Eleven v3 and v4.
Voice cloning: upload a minute of audio for an instant clone, or about 30 minutes for a professional clone.
Voice Library: voice owners share their voices and earn money when others use them.
Dubbing: upload a video and get it translated into other languages in the original speaker's voice.
Agents platform: companies build voice bots that answer calls, connected to their systems, priced per minute.
Everything uses credits on monthly plans, or pay-as-you-go through the API.
overview.valueProposition: Studio-quality voice in any language in seconds, for a tiny fraction of the cost and time of hiring voice actors.

businessModel.summary: ElevenLabs sells monthly subscriptions with credits to creators and small businesses, and usage-based or enterprise contracts to companies and developers. Voice agents are charged per minute. Voice Library pays voice owners a share, which grows supply of voices.

revenueStreams.detail: Starter $5, Creator $22, Pro $99, Scale $330 and Business $1,320 a month, each with credits.
Developers pay by characters or credits used.

ElevenReader and other consumer app subscriptions.

businessModel.pricing: Free: about 10,000 credits a month. Starter: $5 a month. Creator: $22 a month. Pro: $99 a month. Scale: $330 a month. Business: $1,320 a month. Enterprise: custom. Agents billed per minute. Prices from elevenlabs.io.
costDrivers: GPU compute to train and run audio models
Payouts to voice owners in the Voice Library
Safety and moderation to stop voice misuse
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Creator subscriber pays $22 a month for about 100,000 credits, roughly 100 minutes of high-quality speech. Generating that audio probably costs ElevenLabs a few dollars of compute, so the margin is good. Voice agents earn per minute; if a company pays around $0.08 to 0.10 per minute and ElevenLabs pays some of that to an AI language model provider and for compute, it still keeps a healthy share. Since ElevenLabs owns its voice models, it keeps more margin than companies that just resell other models.

growth.moat: ElevenLabs leads on voice quality and has its own models, a huge Voice Library and data from millions of users improving the models. Enterprises trust it for safety features. But big labs like OpenAI and Google also make good voices, so it must keep its quality lead.

pmLessons: Quality can be the whole strategy. ElevenLabs won because its voices sounded clearly more human.
Serve both creators and enterprises. Creators bring fame and feedback; enterprises bring large contracts.
Build a two-sided market where you can. Paying voice owners grows the library and keeps them loyal.
Safety is a product feature. Voice cloning without safeguards can destroy trust.
Owning the model protects margins compared with reselling someone else's.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you stop voice cloning from being misused without hurting honest users?
interviewQuestions.hint: List misuse types. Options: voice verification, blocked voices, watermarks, detection tool, limits. Measure misuse and conversion together.

interviewQuestions.question: Should ElevenLabs focus on creators or enterprises?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue, growth, margins and strategic value. Show how creators feed brand and data. Recommend a balance with reasons.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a voice agent product for Indian banks.
interviewQuestions.hint: Users, languages, use cases (balance, card block), compliance, human handover. Define success like resolution rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Users find credits confusing. How would you redesign pricing?
interviewQuestions.hint: Research how users think (minutes, videos). Options: minutes-based plans, rollover, pay-as-you-go. Test with A/B.

interviewQuestions.question: OpenAI launches free voice cloning. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find what is unique: library, dubbing, quality, enterprise tools. Double down; consider pricing; protect key segments.
